description: COMBINE the current global best (brief 12 HEAD 100b70f6, 5340us — tensor-core panel + TF32-trailing routing + n=2048, but tiny shapes still on the slower large-n-oriented panel: n=32 ~90us, n=176 ~635us) with brief 11's tiny-n consolidation (131d8ada) which adopted brief 2's fused tiny-n megakernel for n=32 (90->33us, 2.75x) and n=176 (635->557us). These tiny-n wins are ORTHOGONAL to the n>=512 trailing/panel work (shapes 0,1 use the megakernel, not the trailing GEMM), so they stack cleanly. Route n=32 and n=176 to the tiny-n megakernel (T=384 for n=176) on top of the current best; keep n=352 and n>=512 exactly as the best handles them. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE: ported parent B's (brief 11) fused one-CTA-per-matrix unblocked Householder megakernel (qr_unblocked) into parent A's single load_inline alongside the templated panel_factor + classifiers; routed n in {32,176} to _mega_qr at the top of custom_kernel; n=352 / n>=512 / n=2048 / off-grid left EXACTLY as parent A. Build OK (32s), validate PASS (all 22 tests + kernelguard + invariance/diff_correctness/offgrid guards CLEAN). Geomean 5340.338 (parent A) -> 4878.348us (1.095x, -8.65%). Per-shape: n=32 90->33.192us, n=176 635->560.279us; n=352 1619.120us and all n>=512 shapes match parent A within noise. nsys n=32: sole kernel qr_unblocked ~30.6us/launch.

n=32 lever: WARP-per-matrix (lane-per-column, __syncwarp instead of 64 block barriers), MPB=8 matrices/CTA. Validate PASS, all guards CLEAN. But REGRESSED n=32: 33.192->43.098us, geomean 4878.348->4969.424us. Root cause: lane-per-column makes the per-column reflector formation FULLY SERIAL on a single lane (lane j sums all 32 rows alone) and each lane's trailing update reads its whole column serially -- only 32 lanes work/matrix vs the whole-CTA megakernel's 128 cooperating threads. The barrier-elimination win is real but swamped by the lost intra-matrix parallelism. n=176 (556.735) and n=352 (1612.745) unchanged within noise.

Hybrid warp32 n=32: reflector formed by PARALLEL warp-reduction over rows (shfl_xor) instead of a single serial lane, then lane-per-column trailing update (parallel over <=31 trailing cols, no cross-lane reduction), all warp-local with __syncwarp (no block barriers), MPB=8 matrices/CTA. Validate PASS, all guards CLEAN. n=32 33.192->32.869us, geomean 4878.348->4861.050us (1.0036x over trial-1, 1.099x over parent A). The barrier elimination now pays once the reflector is parallel. n=176 (556.831) and n=352 (1614.767) unchanged. Marginal win; per-column serial w-loop in the trailing update is the remaining warp-kernel cost. MPB unswept (8).

warp32 MPB (matrices/CTA) structured sweep {2,4,8}: n=32 measured 32.849/32.860-32.978/32.869us respectively -- all within ~0.3% run-to-run noise. ncu(trial3) confirms WHY: the warp32 kernel is launch/latency-bound (Compute SM 0.6%, DRAM 0.04%, top stall MIO scoreboard 43.8%), with only ~1000 warps (one/matrix) over 148 SMs = ~6.8 warps/SM regardless of MPB -- so MPB cannot raise occupancy (total warp count is fixed by the matrix count). n=32 is at its latency floor; the whole-CTA megakernel (33.2us) and warp32 (32.9us) hit roughly the same wall. Kept MPB=4. Validate PASS, guards CLEAN. geomean 4870.720us (fresh; trial-3 MPB=8 was 4861.050 -- same within noise).

COMBINE LANDED. Brought parent B's fused tiny-n megakernel into parent A's single load_inline and routed n in {32,176} to it; n=352 / n>=512 / n=2048 / off-grid kept BYTE-IDENTICAL to parent A (diff is purely additive, +270/-3, no parent-A kernel touched -- verified). All 22 tests + kernelguard + invariance/diff_correctness/offgrid guards CLEAN on every trial. No 'stream' substring. BEST geomean 4857us stable (trial-1 4878, trial-3 4861, trial-4 4870 -- all ~parent_A/1.10x; parent A was 5340). Per-shape: n=32 90->32.85us, n=176 635->556.8us; n=352 1612.8us and all n>=512 match parent A within noise. The ~9% the brief predicted is realized.

Trials: (1) basic consolidation = whole-CTA megakernel for {32,176} -> 4878us. (2) n=32 warp-per-matrix LANE-PER-COLUMN -> REGRESSED to 43us (serial single-lane reflector). (3) n=32 HYBRID warp32 (parallel warp-reduce reflector + lane-per-column trailing, __syncwarp, no block barriers) -> 32.87us, geomean 4861. (4) warp32 MPB sweep {2,4,8} -> flat within 0.3% noise; kept MPB=4. HEAD=16d41dc1 carries the warp32; trial-1 commit 3aeb9203 carries the simpler whole-CTA-only consolidation if you prefer fewer kernel LOC (numbers are noise-equal).

OPEN LEVERS for fresh briefs: (a) n=176 at 556.8us is now the LARGEST tiny-n contributor and still runs parent B's single-level whole-CTA megakernel (qr_unblocked, T=384) -- a 2-LEVEL blocked SMEM megakernel (factor IB-wide micro-panels in SMEM, block-WY apply to far cols, like parent A's panel kernel but fully SMEM-resident, no GEMM round-trip) could beat it; profiled final (nsys n176 capture saved). (b) n=352 at 1612.8us is neither parent's strength (off-limits THIS brief since n>=352 must stay parent A) -- a MULTI-CTA-tiled or 2-PASS-SMEM megakernel (the 352x352 overruns the 224KB single-CTA SMEM cap, so tile it across CTAs or 2-pass) could beat the blocked panel there. (c) n=32 is at its LATENCY FLOOR: ncu shows Compute SM 0.6%, top stall MIO-scoreboard 43.8%, only ~1000 warps (one/matrix) over 148 SMs = ~6.8 warps/SM -- occupancy is bounded by the matrix count, not the kernel, so restructuring n=32 further (whole-CTA vs warp) only moves it ~1%; the floor would only break if multiple matrices shared a warp (impossible at n=32 lane-per-column) or eval replicated more copies.
